fields.title: Medulloblastoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Medulloblastoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Medulloblastoma is an aggressive brain tumour that occurs most often in children. This cancer affects the back of the skull and can spread to other parts of the central nervous system. In Israel, patients with medulloblastoma are offered many-sided and innovative approaches to treatment, aimed at maximising the chances of recovery and minimising long-term side effects.

Diagnosis of medulloblastoma

  1. Laboratory tests
    Include a full blood count and other tests to assess general health and identify possible markers of inflammation or infection.
  2. MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) of the brain
    The main diagnostic method, producing high-resolution images of the tumour.
  3. Lumbar puncture
    Taking a sample of cerebrospinal fluid to detect cancer cells that may be spreading through the central nervous system.
  4. Biopsy
    Carried out where it is necessary to determine the type of tumour and its genetic characteristics precisely.
  5. Neurophysiological examination
    May be used to assess the functional state of the nervous system.

Treatment of medulloblastoma

  1. Surgery
    The aim of the operation is to remove as much of the tumour as possible. Surgery is often the first step in comprehensive treatment.
  2. Radiotherapy
    Used after surgery to destroy remaining cancer cells. Israel uses advanced radiotherapy techniques that reduce the risk of side effects as far as possible.
  3. Chemotherapy
    Given before and/or after radiotherapy to fight the tumour throughout the body.
  4. Targeted therapy
    Where the tumour has particular genetic mutations, specific medicines directed at those mutations may be used.
  5. Immunotherapy
    A relatively new approach to treating certain forms of medulloblastoma, aimed at stimulating the immune system to fight the tumour.

Why patients choose Israel

  • Highly qualified specialists
    Israeli neurosurgeons, oncologists and radiologists have an international reputation and extensive experience in treating medulloblastoma.
  • An individual approach
    Every treatment plan is drawn up with the patient's age, the stage of the disease, the genetic features of the tumour and the patient's general health in mind.
  • Advanced technology
    Treatment uses the most modern medical technologies, including precision diagnostics and minimally invasive surgery.
  • Comprehensive support
    Psychological, social and rehabilitation support is provided to patients and their families at every stage of treatment.

Treatment of medulloblastoma in Israel offers a comprehensive and individual approach aimed at achieving the best possible outcome while preserving patients' quality of life.

fields.title: Melanoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Melanoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Melanoma is an aggressive form of skin cancer that can spread quickly to other organs. In Israel, patients with melanoma have access to innovative methods of diagnosis and treatment that combine the latest scientific advances with an individual approach to every case.

Diagnosis of melanoma

  1. Dermoscopy
    Visual examination of suspicious moles or marks on the skin using a special magnifying device.
  2. Biopsy
    Taking a tissue sample for histological examination, the gold standard in diagnosing melanoma.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Genetic testing for the BRAF mutation
    Establishing whether a mutation in the BRAF gene is present, which can affect the choice of treatment and the outlook.
  4. PET-CT and MRI
    Used to assess how far the melanoma has spread in the body and to detect metastases.
  5. Genetic testing
    Examination of the biopsy tissue for mutations that may affect the choice of treatment.

Treatment of melanoma

  1. Surgical removal
    The primary and most effective treatment for melanoma at an early stage.
  2. Sentinel lymph node biopsy
    This method is used to determine how far the cancer has spread. The sentinel node is the first lymph node to which cancer cells may spread from the primary tumour. Identifying and examining it helps doctors establish whether the cancer has spread further and whether additional treatment is needed.
  3. Immunotherapy
    The use of medicines that activate the immune system to fight the cancer cells.
  4. Targeted therapy
    The use of medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells, particularly where certain genetic mutations such as BRAF are present.
  5. Chemotherapy
    May be used in advanced melanoma, although it is less effective than immunotherapy and targeted therapy.
  6. Radiotherapy
    Sometimes used to treat metastases in the brain or other parts of the body.
  7. Clinical trials
    Patients may take part in trials of new medicines and treatments.

Why patients choose Israel

  • Highly qualified specialists: Israel has leading world experts in dermato-oncology and melanoma.
  • An individual approach to treatment: treatment programmes are developed according to the nature of the disease and each patient's needs.
  • Access to innovative therapies: patients can receive the most modern medicines and take part in clinical trials.
  • Multidisciplinary teams: these ensure a comprehensive approach to treatment, combining the knowledge and experience of doctors of various specialities.

Treatment of melanoma in Israel gives patients access to advanced medical resources and personalised treatment strategies, which helps achieve the best results and improve the outlook.

fields.title: Ocular melanoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Ocular melanoma is a malignant tumour that develops from the pigment cells within the eyeball. Most often it develops in the uveal tract, which includes the iris, the ciliary body and the choroid. The condition can lead to loss of sight and even spread to other organs, which makes it extremely dangerous.

Diagnosis of ocular melanoma

  1. Detailed review of the medical history:
    • The doctor gathers information about symptoms such as changes in vision, dark spots in the field of view, flashes of light and discomfort in the eye, and reviews the family history.
  2. Visual examination and eye tests:
    • Assessment of visual acuity and examination of the eye to identify abnormalities.
  3. Ophthalmoscopy:
    • Examination of the fundus with a special instrument to assess the state of the optic nerve, the vessels and the retina.
  4. Ultrasound examination of the eye:
    • The use of ultrasound to obtain images of the internal structures of the eye and establish the size and position of the tumour.
  5. Fluorescein angiography:
    • Injection of a contrast medium into a vein to assess the blood supply to the retina and identify abnormal changes.
  6. Optical coherence tomography (OCT):
    • Scanning of the structures of the eye to obtain detailed images of the retina and optic nerve.
  7. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT):
    • Used to assess how far the tumour has spread and to detect metastases in other organs.
  8. Biopsy:
    • Taking a tissue sample from the tumour for histological examination to confirm the diagnosis.
      (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)

Treatment of ocular melanoma

  1. Drug therapy:
    • Immunotherapy: the use of medicines that stimulate the immune system to fight the cancer cells.
    • Cytotoxic drugs: used in chemotherapy to shrink the tumour and suppress its growth.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • Brachytherapy: placing radioactive seeds directly in the tumour for local treatment.
    • External beam radiotherapy: radiation directed at the tumour to destroy the cancer cells.
  3. Surgery:
    • Local resection: removal of the tumour and some of the surrounding tissue.
    • Enucleation: complete removal of the eyeball in the case of large tumours or where there is a risk of spread.
  4. Laser therapy:
    • The use of a laser to destroy cancer cells in small, superficial tumours.
  5. Photodynamic therapy:
    • Administration of a light-sensitive agent that is activated by a laser and destroys the cancer cells.

Advantages of treating ocular melanoma in Israel

  1. A high level of professionalism:
    • Israeli doctors have deep knowledge and many years of experience in treating melanoma and other eye conditions.
  2. Modern equipment:
    • Clinics are equipped with advanced diagnostic and treatment devices, which allows highly accurate investigation and effective treatment.
  3. An individual approach:
    • Every patient is given an individual treatment plan that takes account of the nature of the condition and their general health.
  4. Innovative treatments:
    • The use of the most modern methods and medicines, including immunotherapy and photodynamic therapy.
  5. Comprehensive support:
    • Covers not only treatment of the underlying condition but also support for the patient's mental and physical wellbeing during treatment and recovery.

Treatment of ocular melanoma in Israel gives patients access to high-quality medical care and considerably improves both the outlook and their quality of life.

fields.title: Meningioma
fields.bodyHtml:
Meningioma: advanced treatment in Israel

A meningioma is a tumour that develops from the meninges, the membranes covering the brain and spinal cord. Most meningiomas are benign and grow slowly, although some may be aggressive or malignant. In Israel, patients with a meningioma have access to modern methods of diagnosis and treatment and to individually designed treatment programmes.

Diagnosis of meningioma

  1. Laboratory tests
    Include a full blood count and other tests to assess general health and identify possible markers of inflammation or infection.
  2. MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)
    The gold standard in diagnosing meningiomas, allowing detailed study of the size, shape and position of the tumour.
  3. CT (computed tomography)
    May be used to obtain further information about the state of the bones of the skull and spine.
  4. Biopsy
    Carried out where it is necessary to determine the type of tumour and how malignant it is.

Treatment of meningioma

  1. Observation
    Where a benign meningioma grows slowly and causes no symptoms, follow-up with periodic MRI scans may be recommended to monitor the tumour.
  2. Surgery
    The preferred treatment for most meningiomas, allowing the tumour to be removed completely and the patient to be cured. Israel uses both traditional and minimally invasive surgical techniques.
  3. Radiotherapy
    May be used as an alternative to surgery for patients in whom an operation carries a high risk, or to treat tumour remaining after surgery. Advanced methods of radiotherapy are available in Israel, including stereotactic radiosurgery and proton therapy.
  4. Drug therapy
    Currently the subject of active research for malignant meningiomas and those that cannot be treated by surgery or radiotherapy.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach: every case is considered by a team of specialists including neurosurgeons, oncologists and radiologists.
  • Advanced medical equipment: Israeli clinics are equipped with the most modern technology for diagnosing and treating meningiomas.
  • Individual treatment programmes: treatment is planned taking account of every aspect of the patient's health, including age, general condition and preferences.
  • A high standard of medical care: patients receive quality medical care and support at every stage of treatment.

Treatment of meningioma in Israel gives patients access to advanced technology, highly qualified specialists and individual treatment programmes, which offers the best prospects of a successful outcome.
